transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-18
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Daniel Harper (CISO, Oakcrest), Aisha Khan (Head of Cloud Security), Tom Ruiz (Platform Eng Lead)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Maya from Redwood, Liam SE is here, and we have Oakcrest leadership. Thanks for taking the time Daniel, Aisha, Tom.
[00:12] Daniel: Yep, thanks, Maya. We really want to make sure the private deployment pattern is fully compliant with our controls.
[00:17] Aisha: Especially around audit logs, KMS, and tight egress controls.
[00:23] Liam: Great, we planned this as a deep dive. We'll walk through the high-level architecture then zoom into network isolation — ingress/egress — firewalling, as well as our SOC 2/ISO posture and SSO/RBAC integration points.
[00:35] Tom: Sounds good. We have a pretty locked down environment — no public subnets except a bastion for some legacy stuff. We want Redwood in a VPC with strict egress and no direct internet egress from the model nodes.
[00:50] Maya: Perfect, that's aligned with our Private deployment. Quick note — I'll drop the SOC 2 and ISO attestations after the call, and Liam will follow up with the network diagrams and sample IaC.
[01:05] Liam: Kicking off architecture overview — imagine two private subnets: one for control plane components (customer-managed) and one for compute nodes running the runtime. All communication flows over internal interfaces. We support VPC peering and PrivateLink and you can optionally use VPN or Direct Connect for on-prem.
[01:30] Daniel: Do you require public IPs on the workloads for model pull or updates? We want zero public egress.
[01:36] Liam: No, model artifacts can be pulled via S3 endpoints or internal artifact repo — we support S3 VPC endpoints so no public egress. For updates, we have an orchestrated sync that goes through your artifact repository.
[01:50] Aisha: How do you handle outbound telemetry and audit logs? We need them to land in our logging account.
[01:57] Liam: Audit logs and telemetry can be forwarded to your logging pipeline via a private endpoint. We ship structured audit events — auth events, inference request metadata (redacted PII by default), and admin actions. Logs can be delivered over a secured, mutually authenticated channel to your log collector.
[02:15] Tom: Are the audit logs buffered locally? We have constraints on retention and we run our own SIEM.
[02:22] Liam: Yes, logs are buffered and encrypted at rest. You can configure retention in the runbook; we recommend forwarding in near real-time but we can store a time-limited buffer on the control plane for replay if network is disrupted.
[02:40] Daniel: Encryption — we need all keys under our KMS. Do you support customer-managed keys and HSM integrations?
[02:46] Maya: Short answer: yes. For Private deployments, you can bring-your-own KMS. We integrate with cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) and can support external HSM via standard APIs. All disk and object storage encryption uses CMKs you control.
[03:05] Aisha: And are secrets rotated automatically or on our schedule?
[03:09] Liam: Both options. We have automated rotation hooks that can sync with your key policies. You can also trigger manual rotations. Rotation events are recorded in audit logs.
[03:20] [crosstalk] Tom: Sorry — just to clarify — are the model KV caches ever stored unencrypted?
[03:27] Liam: No, KV cache pages and any on-disk spill are encrypted with your CMK. In-memory caches of course reside in RAM and aren't persisted unless configured.
[03:40] Daniel: Network isolation specifics — we want to prevent lateral movement between compute nodes and our other data plane.
[03:46] Liam: We recommend dedicated subnets with strict security group rules and NACLs. We also support microsegmentation via host-level policies and optional host-based firewalls. For strict isolation, we advise separate VPCs with VPC peering only to the minimal service endpoints.
[04:05] Aisha: How about ingress? We don't want inbound from internet to model nodes.
[04:10] Liam: Right — ingress is only from your approved control plane IP ranges or private endpoints. Admin access goes through a bastion or a private jump host. For API access from your apps, we recommend internal load balancers or PrivateLink so no public access path is exposed.
[04:28] Tom: Do you have support for NAT-less egress via interface endpoints?
[04:32] Liam: Yes. We support VPC endpoints for S3, Secrets Manager, KMS, and we can route to your SIEM using private link or a peered logging VPC. That avoids NAT gateways.
[04:45] Daniel: Firewalling and packet filtering — do you recommend network ACLs, security groups, or a combination?
[04:52] Liam: Defense in depth — security groups for instance-level controls, NACLs for subnet-level, and we ship sample Envoy/L7 proxy templates for additional controls. For regulated environments we also recommend inline IDS/IPS and egress allowlisting.
[05:10] Aisha: On egress allowlisting — we need to ensure the deployment cannot exfiltrate data to third-party endpoints. How granular can you be with allowed egress?
[05:18] Liam: You can lock egress to a set of internal endpoints only. If you need external access for things like telemetry, we can send it to a proxy in your environment or to a pre-approved collector IP. We also provide TLS inspection hooks if you run a corporate proxy.
[05:35] Maya: Note — we'll include a sample egress policy in the deliverables.
[05:40] [10:00] Liam: Moving into identity: SSO and RBAC. We integrate with SAML SSO providers and support SCIM user sync. Role-based access can map to your existing groups.
[10:12] Daniel: Important for us — segregation of duties: admin vs operator vs auditor roles. Can roles be tightly scoped?
[10:18] Liam: Yes, roles are granular. We separate cluster admin, model deployer, financial auditor, support engineer scopes. Audit-only roles have read-only access to logs and metric data.
[10:30] Aisha: Any support for attribute-based access control (ABAC)?
[10:34] Liam: We can do ABAC via integration with your identity provider using claims. For example, department or environment claims can gate operations.
[10:45] Tom: What about service accounts for automated jobs? How are those keys rotated and audited?
[10:49] Liam: Service accounts are issued short-lived tokens via our token broker and can be scoped by audience and duration. Rotations are automated and all token exchanges are logged.
[11:05] Daniel: Let's talk about compliance artifacts — can you provide SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 reports?
[11:11] Maya: For Redwood Private we provide our SOC 2 Type II attestation for the platform, plus a set of control mappings for ISO 27001. For customer-managed deployments we also provide a runbook showing how the control responsibilities split between Redwood and customer.
[11:28] Aisha: That's helpful — we need the control matrix to present to our auditors.
[11:32] Maya: We'll share that matrix after the call.
[11:36] [15:00] Tom: Operationally, patching. If you're running on our cloud/private hardware, how are OS and runtime patches applied?
[15:07] Liam: Patching is coordinated. We provide a maintenance window and use immutable images for compute nodes with automated image promotion. For on-prem we can provide an operator-run image repo and a set of playbooks. All patching events are logged.
[15:25] Daniel: For zero-trust setups, can traffic be mutual mTLS between services?
[15:30] Liam: Yes, service-to-service mutual TLS is supported; certificates can be issued by your PKI or our internal CA if desired. We recommend mTLS plus SPIFFE/SPIRE for workload identity where possible.
[15:47] Aisha: Are there any special considerations for model artifacts that contain regulated data?
[15:52] Liam: We recommend encryption-at-rest with CMK and strict RBAC. For very sensitive models, you can run them in an air-gapped on-prem cluster. We also support on-the-fly tokenization and PII redaction hooks in the inference pipeline.
[16:10] Maya: Also want to call out prefix/KV cache handling — by default we don't persist user data beyond the request lifecycle unless configured. We can redact or not store prefixes per your retention policy.
[16:25] Daniel: Speaking of caches — network egress again — if the runtime reaches out to fetch embeddings or external APIs, how do you control that?
[16:31] Liam: Any outbound calls from the runtime are routed over internal proxies you control. You can intercept and monitor requests. There is also an allowlist for outbound destinations and runtime-level hooks to disable external API calls entirely.
[16:50] [20:00] Aisha: Let's dig into firewalling specifics for on-prem: hardware firewall rules, IDS placement, and segmentation.
[20:08] Liam: For on-prem we recommend placing the runtime in a segmented VLAN, with a firewall ACL controlling north-south traffic. IDS/IPS should inspect traffic between the control plane and compute plane as well as egress paths. If you have a hardened DMZ, admin access should come through a jump host within the DMZ with multi-factor access.
[20:30] Tom: Do you support bringing your own firewall policies as code? We run Terraform and Ansible.
[20:35] Liam: Yes, we provide Terraform modules and example Ansible playbooks for rule sets and security groups. We'll include those in the repo we share.
[20:45] Daniel: Service mesh? Are you opinionated or do you allow Istio/Linkerd?
[20:50] Liam: We support integrating with existing service meshes. For mTLS and observability we can plug into Istio or use a lighter-weight Envoy sidecar depending on your preference.
[21:05] Aisha: What about data residency — can you ensure that data and model weights never leave our selected region?
[21:11] Liam: Yes, you choose the region and we lock storage and compute to that region. For backups and artifacts we can enforce region restrictions and disable cross-region replication.
[21:25] Tom: Backup encryption and key escrow — any multi-party key escrow?
[21:30] Maya: We currently support customer-managed CMKs with key policies that can require rotation approvals. Full multi-party escrow is not baked in but can be architected with your custody solution. We'll put references in the runbook.
[21:45] [25:00] Daniel: About network egress telemetry — are there built-in alerts for unusual egress patterns?
[25:07] Liam: We emit telemetry to your SIEM and can predefine detections for unusual volumes or destinations. We also offer anomaly detection hooks that can push to ops.
[25:20] Aisha: For audit evidence, can you provide immutable logs?
[25:24] Liam: Logs are written to append-only storage and signed — we can deliver to your immutable S3 bucket with object lock enabled for WORM policies.
[25:40] Tom: Performance wise — does encryption or mTLS overhead affect latency significantly?
[25:44] Liam: There is a small CPU overhead for mTLS and encryption, but we optimize kernels and use hardware crypto acceleration where available. We've seen sub-5% latency impact in most workloads; we'll run bench tests in your environment to measure.
[26:05] Maya: We'll include some benchmark artifacts and a checklist to reproduce results.
[26:12] [30:00] Daniel: Can we get clarity on the shared responsibility model? Who's responsible for network controls vs. Redwood's agents?
[30:18] Liam: We'll provide a clear matrix: customer controls VPC, CIDRs, NACLs, host-level OS hardening, and physical network. Redwood controls the runtime application, container images we deliver, and the application-level security controls. Shared items like IAM roles and audit delivery are clearly marked.
[30:38] Aisha: Ok. For compliance we need a copy of that matrix to sign off.
[30:42] Maya: We'll send it.
[30:45] [35:00] Tom: Any gotchas for container escapes or side-channel concerns?
[35:06] Liam: We use container hardening, seccomp profiles, and resource limits. For extra hardening, you can run the workloads in dedicated physical hosts (bare metal) or use hardware enclaves — we can architect that for high assurance workloads.
[35:25] Daniel: And how do you prove isolation to an auditor?
[35:29] Liam: We provide architecture diagrams, configurations, immutable logs, and can coordinate read-only auditor access to the log buckets and a deployment environment snapshot.
[35:45] Aisha: Do you support MFA for admin console?
[35:49] Maya: Yes, MFA enforced via SAML/IdP, and we can enforce conditional access policies.
[35:58] [40:00] Liam: Quick note on ingress filtering — we can apply L7 rules via Envoy to validate content and ensure no sensitive patterns leave the runtime. These rules are pluggable so you can add DLP regexes.
[40:15] Tom: Are there recommended CIDR sizes for the deployment?
[40:18] Liam: Depends on scale. We commonly recommend /20 for small clusters and /16 for larger multi-tenant private deployments to ensure room for scaling subnets and NATs. We'll include examples.
[40:35] Daniel: If we require an air-gapped deployment, what changes?
[40:39] Liam: For air-gapped, all artifacts must be transferred via approved media or internal repo. We provide an on-prem installer and operator, and no external outbound connectivity is required. You handle updates via signed artifacts we push into your repo.
[40:58] Aisha: Great. Anything special about firewalling for GPUs?
[41:02] Liam: GPUs don't change the network model, but drivers and telemetry need to be patched so we recommend host-level controls and restricting SSH to bastion only.
[41:12] [45:00] Maya: We're about halfway — quick recap so far: we'll share SOC 2/ISO artifacts, the control matrix, VPC diagram, Terraform modules, and egress policy samples. We'll also set up a bench run checklist.
[45:25] Daniel: Good. On the bench run — we'd like to validate latency and cost estimates on our target instance types.
[45:31] Liam: We'll collaborate on test harness and model sizes. We'll also include kernel-level optimizations we've tested.
[45:48] Tom: For logging, can we run an initial 48-hour soak to validate retention and volume?
[45:53] Liam: Yes, that's a standard step. We'll coordinate the timeframe.
[46:10] Aisha: Any regulatory edge cases for cross-border backups? We need to ensure backups don't go to a different jurisdiction.
[46:17] Liam: We'll ensure backups are region-locked and disable cross-region replication. We'll document that in the runbook.
[46:30] [50:00] Daniel: Final-ish — legal folks will want to see data locality and data processing agreements. Can you provide the DPIA and DPA templates?
[50:08] Maya: We have DPA templates and DPIA guidance for platform deployments; will share those after the call.
[50:16] Tom: Any demo of the admin console with RBAC we can do for our auditors?
[50:20] Liam: Absolutely — we can run a short demo in a staging environment with read-only auditor accounts. We'll schedule that in the workshop.
[50:35] Maya: Alright, let's capture the specific next steps — we'll send the architecture diagram, SOC artifacts, Terraform modules, example egress rules, and propose dates for the on-prem scoping workshop.
[50:48] Daniel: Thanks, appreciate the thoroughness. This helps us get internal buy-in.
[50:53] Aisha: Quick note — we'll circulate our compliance checklist before the workshop.
[50:58] Maya: Perfect. Any other questions?
[51:03] Tom: One last question — do you support hardware attestation for hosts?
[51:07] Liam: We can integrate with TPM-based attestation and provide attestation reports for node boot. Good for high-assurance use cases.
[51:18] [55:00] Daniel: Ok that covers it. Thanks everyone.
[55:05] Maya: Thanks all. We'll follow up with materials and the action items.
[55:12] Liam: I'll be the point for the bench checklist and network templates.
[55:17] Tom: We'll get the CIDRs and a proposed maintenance window to you by Monday.
[55:22] Aisha: We'll also check whether auditors want direct read-only access or just log delivery.
[55:28] Maya: Great. End meeting.

References shared: Redwood Private security deck (link dropped in chat), SOC 2 attestation (to be sent), Terraform module repo (link to be shared), sample runbook and bench checklist.

Recap / Next steps:
- Maya to share SOC 2 & ISO artifacts + control matrix (by 2026-12-20)
- Liam to provide VPC architecture diagram, sample Terraform modules, egress policy examples, and bench checklist (by 2026-12-22)
- Tom to share Oakcrest CIDR and proxy/jump-host details (by 2026-12-21)
- Schedule on-prem scoping workshop (proposed 2026-12-22)

End of transcript.
